notes: Qal has a second, unrequested sense: the three qal perfect forms (1Kgs.6.29, 6.32, 6.35 -- וקלע) all come from the description of Solomon's temple and mean "carve" (of engraved cherubim/palm-tree/flower reliefs on the walls and doors), not "sling." Strong's own entry for H7049 lists both senses ("to sling; also to carve, as if a circular motion, or into light forms") as one root. Only the qal participle forms (Judg.20.16, the famous "sling a stone at a hair and not miss"; Jer.10.18) support the requested "sling (a stone)" gloss and citation. Kept both under qal per the same stem, since they're the same Strong's number/root, but flagging the split so it's visible rather than silently mislabeling the temple-carving forms as "sling."
